newsitem.title: NORWAY: Hydro submits plan for Oseberg gas line.
newsitem.headline: Hydro submits plan for Oseberg gas line.

text.p: Norsk Hydro ASA said on Friday it had submitted a plan for construction and operation of a gas pipeline to run from the Oseberg field to Statpipe in the Heimdal area of the North Sea.
The plan proposes a 36 inch diameter pipeline with a length of 110 kms. Investment was estimated at around one billion crowns, Hydro said in a statement.

It said there were two alternatives for connection to Statpipe -- to be directly connected to Statpipe just south of the Heimdal platform, or to the riser at the Heimdal platform that already connects to the Statpipe line.
"After a further evaluation of the two solutions a recommendation will be submitted to the (Energy) Ministry before June, 1997," Hydro said.
Oseberg will deliver two billion cubic metres (bcm) of gas per year to Germany's Verbundnetz (VNG) from 2000. The planned Oseberg processing capacity is 10 bcm per year.
The Energy Ministry already has approved plans for a gas processing platform that connects to the existing Oseberg field centre facilities.
The processing platform will operate gas exports from the Oseberg area, which is estimated to hold recoverable gas reserves of 115 billion bcm.
The pipeline will be laid in 1999.

Participants in the Oseberg Gas Transport partnership are Norsk Hydro as operator with 13.68 percent, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) with 64.78 percent, Saga Petroleum ASA with 8.55 percent, Elf Petroleum with 5.77 percent, Mobil with 4.33 percent and Total with 2.88 percent.
